assessment.rationale: Directly measured on this exact configuration rather than inferred, which is why directness is direct and scope_match exact. Risk of bias is medium and reproduction not_attempted deliberately: this is a single nsys capture on a contended host, and profiler overhead and co-tenancy both inflate the idle fraction. The claim is therefore that gaps dominate, not that the number is 43.0%. A second capture on a quiet window is the cheapest way to tighten it.

metrics.name: gpu_busy_fraction
metrics.result: 57.4% of the profiled window had a kernel resident. Measured once, under nsys, on a shared host; the profiler inflates gaps and other tenants were active, so the true idle fraction on a quiet box is bounded above by 43% rather than equal to it.

locators.excerpt: total GPU kernel time 25.83s across a 45s window => 57.4% busy; 102,337 kernel launches over ~179 optimizer steps = ~572 launches/step; 144.3ms of kernel time per step against ~480ms observed step time under the profiler
locators.location: nsys profile prof_steady.nsys-rep, 45s steady-state window captured after a 75s delay, GPU 4

scope.budget: 300 charged training seconds on one H200, scope karpathy_228791f_corrected_bpb_h200_train300s_v2c
scope.model: decoder-only transformer, 8 layers, d_model 512, 4 heads of 128, SSSL window pattern

statement: After the pre-tokenized cache removed the dataloader bottleneck, the H200 still runs no kernel at all for roughly 43% of wall time in the steady-state training window, so the dominant remaining cost is gaps between kernels rather than the speed of any individual kernel.
